So I made my first batch about a week ago. My girlfriend helped and she is a pretty good cook, very well trained and generally competent. So I let her rehydrate the yeast even though it probably wasn't necessary for the recipe. The problem is she definitely killed a good percentage of the yeast in the first batch and I didn't buy a backup. Then the following week we brewed again and it happened again, but fear not I had a spare! Unfortunately we got over excited and wound up adding both yeasts to the nicely aerated wort.

So now comes the fun part. My current batch is bubbling nicely, it's 2 gallons (the first was only 1 gallon). Is it possible to mix the two together and bottle them this weekend? If so when should I mix them? As I bottle or earlier on in the week? It seems like there is too much yeast in the second batch and not enough in the first so maybe mixing them would fix that? I could carefully siphon them into one bucket and not add too much air or containment.

Is this a good idea or am I doing something dumb and crazy??

Did you use the exact same recipe and yeast strain for both batches? I think this would only work if you had the exact same beer in both batches and even then it is risky. Each batch of yeast has fermented in slightly different circumstances (temp, cleanliness, amount of wort etc) and this all leads to a unique flavour. So you would be mixing 2 flavours. Also, the 2 batches of yeast will be at differing strengths and may compete with each other, leading to off flavours.

The general rule of thumb is that once the wort cools and the yeast is added do not add any foreign substances at risk of adding an infection. This would include adding another batch of beer. You may currently have 2 gallons of good beer and one of average. Do you want to risk getting 3 gallons of average beer?
What did she do to kill the yeast?
I think she shocked it while trying to rehydrate it. Possibly by heating it too hot.
What makes you think it was shicked, and what was her process for rehydrating?

Did she use hot tap water or boiled water? If it was just hot tap (for most houses) the yeast were probably fine just a little injured. As Jon mentioned, even if she killed off most of them a dry pack is more than enough for a one gallon batch. It might have just taken a little longer for fermentation to start if the cell count was really low. I'd recommend tasting both batches after fermentation is finished, this is really the only way to know if you want to mix the two batches or not.
she used boiled water that she then let cool for a while. she still hasnt put it in the log book so i dont know any specifics

The thing is, even if you start with too little yeast, yeast reproduces like crazy in wort--so the amount in each batch may be different, but it's unlikely to be that different.

If it was a one gallon batch, it's unlikely it was underpitched if you used a whole pack of yeast, even if she rehydrated WAY too warm (it would have to be around 130°F to really kill most of the yeast).

If they are the same or similar recipes, it's fine to blend them at bottling time--but I'd taste them first. Could be you want them bottled separately to see how each batch turns out. :)
